site.title: PoliteBastART
site.description: Freelance illustrator and street artist based in Croatia. PoliteBastart I Vedran Štimac.

about: After graduating from the Faculty of Economics in Pula, I moved to Ljubljana where I am working on my Ph.D. in political anthropology on the domain of peasant social movements. I have been actively involved in illustration since 2014. I became recognized for my drawing style that successfully combines multiple techniques of illustration with great attention to details and free expression. In addition to the illustration, I’m also doing street art and screen printing.

Main motive and also a channel in my illustrative work is portrait. Through that portrait I'm trying to communicate ideas and life of the person which portrait it is. In each illustration, whether on the wall or on paper, I want to build a story behind it, so every illustration is, in a way, socially engaged. With that engagement, I try to bring a certain social phenomena into public discourse.
exhibitions: Brodac Gallery; Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina
UDAS Gallery; Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina
Open Public University of Poreč, Poreč, Croatia
"Drawing Politics - Drawing of Politics" - Group exhibition
"Drawing Politics - Drawing of Politics" - Group exhibition
International festival of alternative theater PUF - Group exhibition

street_art.name: Mural "Imagine the Better World"
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2025)
text: Painted on the façade of Vidikovac Primary School in Pula, the mural shows a pupil striding forward towards a better future, one shaped by peace, solidarity and prosperity.
Holding the globe close and setting a white dove free, the figure carries the world with care into the time ahead.

street_art.name: Mural of Julije Knifer
street_art.caption: Zagreb, Croatia (2021)
text: Julije Knifer (23 April 1924 – 7 December 2004) was a Croatian abstract painter and a founding member of the 1960s Croatian art collective known as the Gorgona Group.
The central motif of mural is Knifer's art, meander, a geometric form which he had been creating since 1960 in various painting techniques such as print, oil, acrylic paint and collage.

street_art.name: Mural of Antonio Gauchito Gil
street_art.caption: Zagreb, Croatia (2021)
text: Antonio Gauchito Gil was Argentinian "Robin Hood" who lived as an outlaw in the 1800s after refusing to fight in the military in a civil conflict. This legendary Argentinian outlaw became a folk saint because of his deeds – stealing with his gang from the rich and giving to the poor. Today, Gauchito is praised as a „people's saint“, as a protector of the poor, oppressed, and all people who are living on the margins of society.

In the portrait of Antonio Gauchito Gil there are candles (which can very often be found on his shrine), and medallion of San Muerte. Legend says that this medallion saved him from the bullet and certain death.

street_art.name: Mural of "Latinoamerica Lucha"
street_art.caption: Buenos Aires, Argentina (2019)
text: In 2019, in Chile, were huge mass demonstrations against neoliberal policies. Civil protests took place throughout Chile in response to a raise in the Santiago Metro's subway fare, the increased cost of living, privatisation and inequality prevalent in the country.

The mural is drawn on the former prison in Las Barracas barrio, Buenos Aires. Silhouette of the portrait belongs to a native Latin-American woman. Inside the portrait is a woman with a flag of Mapuche people (native people who suffered the most from colonial policies), and the Wiphala - a square emblem commonly used as a flag to represent some native peoples of the Andes that include today's Peru, Bolivia, and parts of Ecuador, Argentina, Chile and Colombia.

street_art.name: Mural of Herbert Marcuse
street_art.caption: Krapina, Croatia (2017)
text: Herbert Marcuse was a German-American philosopher, sociologist, and political theorist, associated with the Frankfurt School of critical theory. His most famous book is the „One-dimensional Man“ where he argues in short that no matter if we are workers or bureaucracy, we are all together victims of a consumer society.

On the portrait background is drawn a barcode which generally symbolizes the consumer society, and inside the portrait are white and blue collar workers. It communicates the main idea from his book „One-dimensional Man“.

street_art.name: Mural of Rossana Rossanda
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2021)
text: Rossana Rossanda (1924-2020) was born in Pula, Croatia, during the initial consolidation of Benito Mussolini’s Fascist regime. She was a journalist, writer, feminist, and protagonist of Italian politics. She was a participant in the partisan movement and militant members of the PCI (from where she was expelled because of her critical stance towards USSR authoritarian politics) and the Italian parliament from 1963 to 1968. She made a huge contribution to the founding of the influential paper "Il Manifesto", which remains the most critical daily in Berlusconi’s Italy.

The main motive in the mural is her leaving of this world walking up the stairs into one more just world – a world for she fought through all of her life. The curtains here are made of newspapers „Il Manifesto“, where se was one of main editors, and also one of the founders.

street_art.name: Mural of "Cities for People, Not for Profit"
street_art.caption: Ljubljana, Slovenia (2019)
text: The dominant trend of gentrification and raise of rents due the free market is affecting huge mass of population. Lots of people even in the so-called „developed“ west can't afford a decent housing. Young people are still living with their parents, and those who are considered lucky live with 2 or more roommates. Also, there huge number of people who can't afford even that and are homeless.

In the portrait is a map of Ljubljana with a focus around AKC Metelkova (keyhole is painted on it). The rat symbolizes marginalized, oppressed, and stigmatized citizens who have the "key" of their hometown. It is a question of the moment when they will use that "key" and fight dominant urbanistic practices guided by the profit logic.

street_art.name: Mural of "Solidarity with The People of Palestine"
street_art.caption: Sisak, Croatia (2021)
text: For decades, systematic oppression and ethnic cleansing of the population of Palestine have been carried out by the State of Israel. From land grabbing, forcible relocation of people, disruption of electricity and water supplies, abolition of exchange of goods and services (eg. ban on import of Covid vaccines for medical staff), to rocketing the Gaza Strip in which only in 2021 lost its life 256 people (66 children and 40 women). In moments when there is injustice, it is important not to be silent about it, because in that way we are standing on the side of the oppressor.

This mural was painted on a residential building in Sisak - as a call for an end to Israeli aggression, solidarity with the people of Palestine and hope for a brighter, more peaceful and freer future for all people in Palestine and Israel who are victims of violence and daily injustice. The portrait silhouette belongs to Leila Khaled, Palestinian activist and intellectual.

street_art.name: Mural of "Solidarity with Rojava Revolution"
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2020)
text: The Rojava conflict, also known as the Rojava Revolution, is a political upheaval and military conflict taking place in northern Syria, known among Kurds as Western Kurdistan or Rojava. A new kind of society is being built in Syria, but it's not one you would expect. Surrounded by deadly bands of ISIS and hostile Turkish forces, the people living in Syria's Rojava cantons are carving out one of the most radically progressive societies on the planet today.

Dominant colours in the mural are the red, green and yellow which are the colours of the Rojava's flag. Also, there are three portraits of woman, which symbolize solidarity among Syrian woman and feminism (the bastion of Rojava democratic confederalism).

street_art.name: Mural of "Fallen Industry"
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2020)
text: Back 20 years ago, Pula was industrial city. Shipyard and various factories provided a decent life to the half of the city population. Nowadays, the dominant trend of deindustrialization, and economy based only on tourism, is devastating for welfare of Pula's citizens.

This street art piece is dedicated to shipyard Uljanik which was one of the last bastions of Pula's industry. Continuous and ubiquitous sale of public goods in favor of private interests results in an existential crisis for many of us. The modified pattern of Louis Vuitton represents the shipyard as a pure commodity for sale.

street_art.name: Mural of Dragutin Gorjanović Kramberger
street_art.caption: Krapina, Croatia (2015)
text: Dragutin Gorjanović-Kramberger was a Croatian geologist, paleontologist, and archeologist. His most famous archeological discovery was neanderthal skull „type C“ on Hušnjak Hill near Krapina.

In this street art piece we can see the exact Neanderthal skull „type C“ as a mask on Gorjanović's face. The mural was painted in Krapina because the importance of heritage he left with work during life.

street_art.name: Mural of Sean Connery
street_art.caption: Umag, Croatia (2016)
text: Sir Sean Connery was a Scottish actor. He was the first actor to portray fictional British secret agent James Bond on film, starring in seven Bond films between 1962 and 1983.
In this street art piece, a portrait of him acting in the movie “From Russia with Love” is shown. Instead of his face there is an opening scene from James Bond movies.
